parsed.explanation: Inside the state, operative protections are strong: statewide gender-identity anti-discrimination, mandated gender-neutral bathrooms, hate-crimes coverage and shield law for care. That does not cancel the unavoidable federal layer: binary passport/visa rules upheld in Nov 2025, visa cable requiring refusal on sex discrepancy and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, federal-facility exclusion, and documented immigration-custody forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse. If outed at entry or in federal custody, severity is major to severe, with contested, partial remedies. Other governments have issued trans-travel advisories.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal binary sex definition; X/mismatched markers stopped for new US passports, existing X valid to expiry. Visa cable: document discrepancy casts doubt on sex -> refuse and seek evidence; suspected wilful misrepresentation may support permanent lifetime fraud ineligibility. Passports confiscated/blocked, travellers stranded; neighbouring citizens detained over visa issues.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration. Civil-liberties suit challenges passport policy; several Jan 2025 orders blocked/enjoined; legal-aid FAQ guidance. State X markers on licences/forms do not govern federal entry.
entry_documents.interaction: State protective documents cannot override federal visa adjudication. Discrepancy at consulate/border can lead to refusal before state protections are ever reached, and a fraud finding follows the traveller.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections policy from 2026 adopted conversion-therapy model: hair cutting, hormone removal, psychiatric drugs; denial of care. Immigration custody: trans men reported forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement, severe sexual abuse. Number of trans prisoners no longer reported from 2025.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented for federal custody. State protections do not apply in federal facilities or custody. No documented pre-emption or refusal by federal custodians.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest or immigration detention moves traveller from state-protected setting into federal custody where documented abuse and care removal apply, negating local recourse.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity. Nationally bans in government buildings in many states, with 4 states making use criminal in certain circumstances and one trespass arrest documented. This state is not documented among ban states.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State: Gender Expression Non-Discrimination Act covers public accommodations since 2019, 2024 constitutional amendment bans gender-identity discrimination, gender-neutral bathrooms mandated since 2021. No state bathroom ban documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: In state/private settings congruent access is protected; in federal buildings, federal exclusion governs regardless of state law. State law does not cancel federal facilities exposure.

care_services.exposure: Federal orders label minors' gender-affirming care 'chemical and surgical mutilation', freeze funding, propose barring public insurance for under-18 care, subpoena hospital records. Emergency care in federal settings may involve birth-sex records.
care_services.protection: State shield law/executive order from 2023, 2023 law barring enforcement of out-of-state custody-removal and child-abuse treatment, city bar on using resources to investigate care. Documented as protecting patients/providers travelling for care.
care_services.interaction: Shield protects care obtained in-state from out-of-state enforcement, but does not document protection against federal funding, investigation or custody actions. Adult visitor care continuity is stronger than a minor's federal exposure.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal framing: removal of gender-ideology materials, forbidden terms, counterterrorism strategy prioritising 'radically pro-transgender' groups, cash-reward memo using 'radical gender ideology', EO directing investigation/prosecution of teachers facilitating minor social transition. 66% poll support for birth-sex on documents.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Federal hate-crimes statute covers gender identity; state Hate Crimes Act covers gender identity/expression since 2019, panic defence repealed 2019, pre-2021 harassing penal provision repealed. Several federal orders enjoined; courts active.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State and federal enforcement point opposite directions. Federal threat-framing raises outing and investigation probability at national level; state law provides local recourse but no documented immunity from federal action.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal orders target schools and teachers using preferred names/pronouns for minor transition, threaten funding and criminal prosecution; youth-care bans nationally in 27 states. One county in this state bans trans athletes in county facilities, 2025 ruling found no clear anti-discrimination violation, lawsuit pending.
minors_guardians.protection: State shield bars out-of-jurisdiction custody enforcement and law-enforcement cooperation; anti-bullying law covers gender identity; conversion therapy on minors banned since 2019; parental-consent self-affirmation for birth-certificate change under 17 is resident-facing.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian travelling with minor can access shield-protected care in-state, but federal school/funding investigations and the county sports ban remain documented exposures not cancelled by shield. No documented federal pre-emption of shield.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Not documented. No trans-specific violence incident or rate in this state is documented; general polling is LGBTQ-general, not trans-specific. Airport screening described as invasive and outing-risk.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crimes law, anti-discrimination enforcement, repeal of provision historically used to harass trans people, and 'Most Protective' tier ranking suggest functioning local recourse, but ranking is bill-based not incident-based.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local police interaction in-state is documented as protected; federal border/police screening is the documented street-level risk and is separate from state policing.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport restriction upheld by Supreme Court Nov 2025; other orders remain in litigation, outcome time-dependent. Custody abuse remedies not documented. Lack of trans-specific violence data.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active lawsuits, injunctions on several orders, state Division of Human Rights regulations, hate-crimes statute, legal-aid guidance. Remedies exist but contested and uneven across federal vs state actors.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are strongest in-state for discrimination/care and weakest at federal entry, facilities and custody—the stages every visitor must pass. Documented protection in one stage does not cure exposure in another.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: routine document-linked exposure at checkpoints, detention/humiliation and denial possible, imprisonment unlikely, remedies slow/contested. Here federal visa/facility layer plus documented custody abuse makes consequences more severe than 0.45-A, while state protections are stronger.

Similar on entry: extended secondary screening on document discrepancy, discretionary refusal/return, slow appeal. Higher than this case on remedy certainty; lower here because a suspected misrepresentation can trigger permanent lifetime ineligibility and federal facilities/custody add tier-1 exposure.

Higher than 0.65-A: there courts reliably ordered release, complaint produced apology/compensation, no imprisonment. Here passport restriction was upheld, entry refusal is instructed, and custody abuse is documented, so local remedy does not reliably restore the traveller.

Well below 0.75-C, where detention is brief, counsel and compensation are documented and entry on matching markers is accepted. Here the operative federal regime, not state law, governs entry and facilities.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime is bifurcated: state law creates a documented protective operating regime for facilities, services and care, including shield for travelling families. Federal law creates unavoidable entry screening, document-mismatch refusal with possible lifetime fraud finding, federal-facility exclusion, and severe documented custody harm. Under V3, state protection does not cancel federal entry/facility/custody exposure. Severity if outed federally is major-severe, probability is universal at border, remedies are partial and litigated. That places the case below Reduced Risk, near the 0.45 anchor, lifted only by strong in-state protections.
